initialization_sequence: 1. Hold RESET_n LOW. Ramp the supplies in the defined order: VDD1 (~1.8 V), VDD2H / VDD2L, and VDDQ (0.5 V).
2. Once supplies are stable, deassert RESET_n (drive HIGH) and wait the defined reset-exit time.
3. Start the quarter-speed differential master clock CK_t/CK_c and allow it to stabilize.

4. Program mode registers via MRW (two CA cycles each: MA[6:0] then OP[7:0]): operating frequency set point (FSP), Read/Write Latency (RL/WL), bank mode (BG/16B/8B), WCK ratio, link-ECC / DBI enables, ODT / output-driver impedance, Vref(ca)/Vref(dq).
5. Run ZQ calibration against the external reference resistor (start/latch via MPC).
6. Perform the initial WCK2CK synchronization (CAS with WS_FS) and train DQ/RDQS read timing and WCK write timing (DFE / equalization) for the active frequency set point.
7. Device is ready for normal operation.
reset_sequence: 1. Assert RESET_n LOW; device enters reset state (mode registers cleared, outputs Hi-Z).
2. Re-run the initialization sequence from step 2.
row_open_sequence: 1. Issue ACT-1 (row high bits, bank / bank group) on the CA bus (two CA transfers).
2. Issue ACT-2 (row low bits) to complete opening the row.
3. Wait tRCD before the first column command to that bank.
read_sequence_BL16: 1. Open the target row (ACT-1, ACT-2; wait tRCD).
2. Issue CAS carrying WS_RD to synchronize the DRAM's WCK to CK for an immediately following read.
3. Issue RD with the column / bank / bank-group address (and AP for auto-precharge if desired).
4. Wait the programmed Read Latency (RL). The DRAM enables and drives RDQS edge-aligned with DQ.
5. Capture 16 beats from DQ on both edges of RDQS; decode Read Link ECC and DBI as configured.
6. Optionally issue PRE after tRTP, or use RD with auto-precharge.
read_sequence_BL32: 1-2. Same as BL16 read up to the CAS(WS_RD) sync.
3. Issue RD32; optionally specify a starting position within the 32-word-aligned burst via C0 / B3.
4. Capture 32 beats on DQ framed by RDQS.
write_sequence_BL16: 1. Open the target row (ACT-1, ACT-2; wait tRCD).
2. Issue CAS carrying WS_WR to synchronize the DRAM's WCK to CK for an immediately following write.
3. Issue WR (or MWR for masked write) with the column / bank / bank-group address.
4. Wait the programmed Write Latency (WL). Drive WCK; drive 16 beats of DQ (+ DMI for mask / DBI) on both WCK edges; encode Write Link ECC as configured.
5. After tWR, issue PRE; or use WR with auto-precharge.
write_x_sequence: 1. Open the target row and issue CAS(WS_WR) with the WRX (Write-X) option and WXS (write-X select) bit.

2. Issue the write; the DRAM fills the burst with all-zeros (WXS=0) or all-ones (WXS=1) WITHOUT the controller transferring data on the bus — saving the same time as a normal write while saving IO power.
multi_bank_bank_group_sequence: 1. ACT a row in bank group BG0 bank0; respect tRRD_S to a different bank group, tRRD_L within the same bank group; at most 4 ACTs within tFAW.
2. Issue CAS(WS_FS) to free-start WCK for multiple following accesses across multiple banks.
3. RD/WR across banks honouring tCCD_S (different bank group) and tCCD_L (same bank group).
4. PRE (per-bank) or PREab (all-bank) when done; wait tRP.
refresh_sequence: 1. Track elapsed time since last refresh; target average tREFI for the current temperature range (read via MRR temperature status).
2. Issue REFab (all-bank) when all banks are idle and wait tRFCab; OR issue REFpb (per-bank, round-robin bank order) and wait tRFCpb while accessing other banks.
3. If RFM (Adaptive Refresh Management) is enabled, issue RFM commands per the activation-count policy for Rowhammer reliability.
4. Execute all required refreshes before entering self-refresh / deep sleep.
self_refresh_entry_exit_sequence: 1. Bring the device to a refreshable idle state (banks precharged).
2. Issue SRE over the CA bus (no CKE). The DRAM generates internal refresh; CK may be stopped per the defined window.
3. To exit: restart CK if stopped, issue SRX (or rely on CS activity), and resynchronize WCK (WCK2CK) before the next transfer.
4. For Deep Sleep Mode (DSE bit set at entry): on exit, re-run the full initialization sequence.
dvfs_frequency_change_sequence: 1. Quiesce traffic; precharge banks as required.
2. Switch the active Frequency Set Point (FSP) via mode register; DVFSC selects VDD2H or VDD2L for the new operating point.
3. Change the CK / WCK frequency; re-run ZQ calibration and WCK2CK synchronization; retrain DQ/RDQS read and WCK write timing with the FSP-specific RL/WL/ODT/Vref/DFE settings.
4. Resume traffic at the new operating point.
power_down_entry_exit_sequence: 1. Issue a power-down entry command over the CA bus (PD bit). There is NO CKE pin.
2. The power-down mode lasts until the chip select (CS) signal next goes high.
3. On CS activity, the device exits power-down and resumes; resynchronize WCK before the next transfer.
